gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-serif-hentaig: Vintage muscle: Woodgod cuts wide channels into every bowl, with lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals' height. Noto Serif Hentaigana follows with gentle stroke modulation and open jaws.
gen-unbounded-fs-epilogue: Wide-set, oversized lowercase bodies give Unbounded a sprawling, friendly look that spreads across the line right away. Epilogue's sans lettering runs as thin neon-tube wire, curvy and unclamped.
gen-unbounded-general-sans: Unbounded spreads its oversized lowercase wide, giving every word a friendly, contemporary stance before the eye moves on. Its sweep rewards a few big words; General Sans keeps sans-serif curves smooth.
gen-butcherman-inter: Inter lays out smooth, tube-like lines, its counters gaping like a hollow reed cut open and its lowercase generous. Inter's openness against Butcherman's pinched, slot-like apertures is the whole drama.
gen-butcherman-poppins: Raw and dark, Butcherman keeps every letter apart, with a dominant x-height. Poppins then glides through a paragraph, its rope-loose curves never knotting and no swing between heavy and light snagging the eye.
gen-butcherman-roboto-slab: Dark and raw, Butcherman keeps its letters from ever touching, with small slot-like apertures. Roboto Slab reads steadily over paragraphs, its slab-serif middle zone dense and its throats open.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-julius-sans-one: Arkhip floats its letters well apart, with a c as open as a bent paperclip and no stroke modulation. Julius Sans One drifts alongside, its sans lowercase nearly capital height and just as loosely spaced.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega reads like one nib drew everything. Arkhip is best at floating geometric display lettering, while Lexend Mega's near-capital lowercase and visible c gaps handle the sans-serif reading.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-lexend-zetta: Arkhip's letters float well apart, each c open like a bent paperclip. Lexend Zetta cuts constant-width strokes like ribbon and tracks wide, and that shared looseness of spacing is the pair's real hook.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-montserrat-alternat: Rounded and chalk-board-like, the body text crowds its lowercase up toward the capital line. Montserrat Alternates handles that dense reading, while Arkhip is best left to a few spaced-out display words.
